purpose: Somatropin is a man-made version of the natural growth hormone your body produces. It is used to help children who are not growing properly due to low growth hormone levels or certain medical conditions. It is also used in adults whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone, and in some other conditions like Turner syndrome or Prader-Willi syndrome.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a hormone called growth hormone in the brain, which tells your bones and muscles to grow and helps control how your body uses energy. Somatropin works just like your natural growth hormone by sending the same signals to your body. This helps promote growth in children and helps adults maintain healthy muscle mass, bone strength, and metabolism.
common_side_effects: Swelling, pain, or redness at the injection site. You may also notice swelling in your hands or feet, joint or muscle aches, headaches, or mild numbness and tingling. Some children may experience hip or knee pain. These side effects often improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have cancer or a history of cancer, as growth hormone can potentially stimulate cell growth. Do not use this medication if you are seriously ill or have had recent major surgery without talking to your doctor first. People with diabetes should monitor their blood sugar closely, as somatropin can raise blood sugar levels. Children with Prader-Willi syndrome who are overweight or have breathing problems need extra monitoring. Never share your injection pen or needles with anyone else.
typical_dosing: Somatropin is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) once daily, usually at bedtime, since your body naturally releases growth hormone during sleep. The dose is carefully calculated based on your body weight or body surface area and is set individually by your doctor. Your doctor will start you at a low dose and slowly adjust it based on how your body responds and your lab results. Always follow your doctor's exact dosing instructions.
